seo_description: Solo audio designer on a 4-player racing game. First real team project — procedural MetaSounds engine, priority-based mix, and team voice recording in 11 weeks.
hero.title: Not Today, Darling!
hero.subtitle: Solo Audio Designer. 5-person team. 11 weeks. A life lesson in disguise.
concept.hook: I thought this would be about making a game. It turned out to be a life lesson.
concept.p1: Not Today, Darling! is a chaotic 4-player side-scrolling racer where grannies smash their way to victory on go-karts. We had 11 weeks and total creative freedom — everyone pitched ideas on a whiteboard, we circled what excited us, and built from there. I was the only audio person, handling everything from the procedural engine sound to the final mix.
concept.p2: This was my first time working with animators, developers, and artists on something real. There were arguments. Conflicts of interest. People wanting different things. Before this, nobody at DAE had ever questioned my work — suddenly everything was up for debate. It was frustrating and eye-opening. I learned how collaboration actually works: the fights, the compromises, the deadlines you can't miss because other people depend on you.
concept.p3: At the very end, I recorded everyone from the team doing granny voices — reactions to collisions, power-ups, overtakes. Pick a character color and you're hearing one of us. A little keepsake from a project that, under the surface, was never really about the game. It was about learning to ship together. And it's the reason I was ready for Shadow Frames.
systems.engine.title: Procedural Go-Kart Engine
systems.engine.desc: My first serious MetaSounds project. RPM, throttle, and load drive the engine sound in real-time — no baked loops. It responds to player input frame by frame. I was learning MetaSounds as I went, so the code wasn't pretty, but the engine sounds right.
systems.mix.title: Priority-Based Mix
systems.mix.desc: 4 players means 4 engines, 4 sets of power-ups, collisions, and voices all at once. Sound Classes with priority levels keep the local player's audio on top. Attenuation presets push distant karts into the background. Without this, the mix turns to mud.
systems.voices.title: Character Voices
systems.voices.desc: Granny voice lines recorded with the team — each character color is a different team member. Reactions to collisions, power-ups, and overtakes, implemented as randomized Sound Cues with cooldown timers so they don't spam.
challenge1.title: Mix Clarity with 4 Players
challenge1.hard: 4 karts, 4 engines, power-ups and collisions all playing at once on top of character voices. Everything collapsed into noise. Players couldn't tell what was happening to their own kart. I had no prior experience managing a mix this busy.
challenge1.did: Built a Sound Class hierarchy with priority levels. The local player's kart always sits on top. Distant karts get attenuated and ducked. Power-up and collision sounds run through concurrency limits, so only the most relevant ones play. First time doing any of this — it worked.
challenge2.title: Procedural Engine That Feels Right
challenge2.hard: MetaSounds was completely new to me. Procedural synthesis can sound sterile and disconnected from what's happening on screen. The engine had to respond instantly to throttle changes and feel like it's actually powering the kart.
challenge2.did: Mapped RPM, throttle position, and load directly to MetaSounds parameters. Added pitch smoothing so sudden input changes don't cause jarring jumps. The result tracks player input frame by frame.
